pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Aims - Godolphin and Latymer
pageCache.text:
Ethos & Aims
Godolphin and Latymer is a modern and forward-looking school with a strong heritage and ethos that shapes the character and heart of our school. The story of our philanthropic origins, and of Head Mistress Dame Joyce Bishop’s pledge in 1945 ‘to best share the task of educating a nation’, is celebrated every year on our birthday. It is this ethos that underpins our commitment to our means-tested bursary programme: we would like every bright girl who is offered a place at Godolphin to be able to come, irrespective of her financial background. We welcome pupils from a wide range of different cultures, faiths and backgrounds which creates a unique and dynamic learning environment.
At Godolphin and Latymer, we aim to provide our pupils with an outstanding education. Through the lessons and activities in which they participate, girls learn for life. They develop habits of mind that promote curiosity and initiative, intellectual rigour and independence of thought, reflective learning and flexible thinking, the ability to maintain an open mind and to reach a balanced judgement. They achieve excellent examination results and follow the higher education pathway of their choice at leading institutions in the UK and beyond.
At Godolphin and Latymer, we recognise that all our students are different and we aim to provide each one with a stimulating and enjoyable education. We offer an exciting range of intellectual, creative and physical challenges and opportunities, encouraging the development of individual passions and particular skills alongside the self-esteem and confidence with which to succeed in unfamiliar situations.
At Godolphin and Latymer, our long history of providing education for pupils from a wide range of backgrounds creates an enriching and inclusive atmosphere. Within this principled, caring and friendly community, girls learn to lead, to work together for mutual benefit, to communicate clearly and to forge firm friendships.
At Godolphin and Latymer, we encourage students to learn about local, national and global issues and in so doing we believe they become considerate, compassionate and courageous young women who fully expect to take active responsibility for the community and the environment in which they live, as well as for themselves, both now and in the future.

Head’s Welcome Dr Frances Ramsey
When I welcome visitors to Godolphin and Latymer, they often comment on the warm, friendly and supportive atmosphere and the creative and enthusiastic energy of the girls. This is a school where individual talents are nurtured and championed and where students are encouraged to develop their own passions and interests; there really is no typical Godolphin girl!
We take pride in the school’s longstanding reputation for academic excellence, but there is much more to life here than simply our headline achievements. We are ambitious and innovative in our approach to teaching and learning to best equip and inspire our students to flourish in the outside world. For our Sixth Form pupils there is the choice of the A Level or International Baccalaureate pathway and, from the very beginning of a student’s time at the school, the curriculum is both broad and deep. Our G&L Futures programme aims to develop the important skills our students will need as young adults such as resilience, leadership, collaboration, communication, creative-thinking and entrepreneurship. Beyond the classroom there is a huge amount going on and the range of activities and interests pursued by the girls, with such boundless commitment and energy, never ceases to amaze me.
I hope that our website gives you a flavour of life at Godolphin and Latymer. However, it is by visiting us that you will gain the strongest impression of our unique atmosphere and ethos, and I do very much look forward to extending a warm welcome to you in the near future.
"Erudite and incisive, Dr Ramsey initially thought she would become a university lecturer but ended up spending her entire career in central London secondary schools. ‘She runs a tight ship and has a great team in place,’ parents told us."

pageCache.text:
Ancient World Breakfast Club
The Godolphin and Latymer Ancient World Breakfast Club (AWBC) was established in 2005 as a weekly lecture series to promote the study of the ancient world among members of the wider community. Since that time, interest has grown considerably – membership is currently around 200 people – and the club has developed a fine reputation for attracting distinguished speakers on many and varied topics to do with the ancient world. Undaunted by the early hour – or perhaps lured by the promise of yoghurt and muesli, croissants and coffee – enthusiasts of all ages join us at 7.30am for an 8.00am start, each Friday of term for their weekly dose of intellectual edification. No prior knowledge of Greek, Latin, or the classical world is required. For further information, please email: office@godolphinandlatymer.com
For more information about the club, including information for members (and prospective members), please choose one of the links below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Autumn Sunshine and Inspiring Landscapes are the Backdrop for Art Department Trip to Worthing - Godolphin and Latymer
pageCache.text:
News Autumn Sunshine and Inspiring Landscapes are the Backdrop for Art Department Trip to Worthing 08.10.2026
A Level and IB Visual Arts students, alongside their teachers, spent the day in Worthing exploring the beach and surrounding landscape. Throughout the day, students used film-based manual cameras to experiment with photography, alongside observational drawing and a stamping process to capture impressions of the environment.
More broadly, students used the landscape as an opportunity to consider the themes underpinning their individual enquiries from a different perspective, taking them beyond the confines of the classroom and placing them within a new context. This shift in environment encouraged deeper levels of thinking and prompted inventive approaches to recording and responding to their surroundings.
A fish and chip lunch on the pier, combined with a morning and afternoon spent in glorious autumn sunshine, created a relaxed and reflective day of creative activity by the sea.

pageCache.pageTitle: Speech and Drama - Godolphin and Latymer
pageCache.text:
Speech and Drama Trinity Champion Centre
Speech and Drama is offered as an additional option to all students. More than 350 students each year take Speech and Drama lessons. These sessions are hugely popular and help to build confidence, develop individual performance skills and to provide an opportunity to practise communication and presentation skills – essential life-skills for the world of work and beyond!
Students are taught in small groups in forty minute lessons and follow the Trinity College London Speech and Drama courses, working towards optional examinations at the end of the school year. Students begin at Grade 3 and work towards Grade 8 in the Sixth Form. They perform play extracts, poetry, book extracts and public speeches and each grade includes an expressive reading and a short interview task. Trinity College exams have no set texts so enable each student to develop a bespoke exam programme, reflecting their own skills, interests and experiences.
We have been named as a Trinity Champion Centre for the sixth year running! This is awarded for our extensive programme of Speech and Drama study and for our consistently outstanding exam results.

pageCache.text:
News Career Insights into the Art World with Art Advisor, Sophie Singh 08.10.2026
On Tuesday, the History of Art department and Sixth Form art historians welcomed Sophie Singh to speak about careers in the art world. Sophie is an Art Advisor with wide experience in curating, marketing and consulting, working in both the art market and with public art institutions like the Tate. She spoke about the structure of the art world, career ladders within it, and prospects for the Arts sector amidst the challenge of AI. The Godolphin students present asked several great questions and went away with invaluable insights into the opportunities, pitfalls and rewards of choosing a career working with art.

pageCache.pageTitle: From Fintech to Healthtech: Software in the Age of AI: Online Talk with Serkan Kutan - Godolphin and Latymer
pageCache.text:
News From Fintech to Healthtech: Software in the Age of AI: Online Talk with Serkan Kutan 09.10.2026
On Thursday 8 October, we welcomed Serkan Kutan, a technology expert whose career has included Microsoft, Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Zocdoc, and Zelis, and who has previously served as the CTO of Amwell, to give an inspiring online talk about his career journey and the future of software engineering to the excited computer scientists, software engineers, and aspiring healthcare/fintech professionals at our school.
The talk was organised by Luna, Lower Sixth, and students were fascinated to hear about what these sectors are looking for in terms of skills, especially now that AI plays such a key role in technical jobs. Serkan emphasised the importance a growth mindset to fulfil the the vision of being able to build and create products, and the students learned that in the growing age of AI, it is important to be able to “speak” AI and direct it to make better and bigger things faster.
He also talked through whether a large company or a start-up is the better career choice, and though the answer boiled down to there being no right answer, students were able to grasp a much better understanding of the advantages of both. From start-up environments that provide better opportunities for the builder mindset where you improve and evolve much quicker through building, failing, and iterating more often, to large companies which are generally able to provide better resources for you to build, Serkan inspired everyone to think for themselves and to remember that it is most important to maximise your learning and stretch yourself no matter what environment you are in.
Ending the talk with some advice, Serkan urged our student to have the confidence to be open, flexible, and constantly learning, especially in the current ever-changing world, and to be the person who is able to fluently use the advancements and the technology, and particularly AI, to their advantage rather than treating them as something to be wary of.

pageCache.pageTitle: London School of Economics Debating Competition - Godolphin and Latymer
pageCache.text:
News London School of Economics Debating Competition 13.10.2026
Five debating pairs entered the annual schools competition hosted by students at the London School of Economics on Saturday 10 October. Across topics comparing US and UK universities, ‘clergy-penitent privilege’, the merits of biopics and the best strategy for the US Democrats, all performed with credit. But Elena and Carmen, Year 11 performed particularly well, qualifying for the Silver Final. Despite a spirited case for the feminist movement condemning the ‘tradwife’ fashion, they did not win that round but were nevertheless in the top 6% of the 128 entrants.
Congratulations, Dolphins!

Higher Education and CareersPlanning for the future
Our Higher Education and Careers programme starts in Year 7 as students begin to think about the subject areas that most interest them and discover the wide range of careers that are available to them. Careers education is central to preparing our students for the realities of the workplace and the school engages with the Gatsby Benchmarks in order to provide effective careers guidance. All pupils across the school have access to two key platforms: Unifrog and Morrisby.
In addition, there are a series of microsites which all pupils have access to via their iPads. These cover a wide range of areas related to Higher Education and Careers including:
For relevant year groups, details of internships, work experience opportunities, MOOCs, taster lectures, summer school courses and much more besides, are shared with students so that they can make the most of these opportunities. We also publish a podcast series: The Pod – which features our alumnae who share their higher education and career journeys. This, and much more information about our inspiring alumnae, can be found on the Sixth Form section of the website.

Events
We run several events to augment pupil’s knowledge of the world of work and higher education opportunities:
Careers Evening
Clubs, Societies and Enrichment Opportunities
Our Clubs and Societies attract excellent speakers who allow our students to connect to the world of work, for example Lord Vaizey addressed the Politics Society discussing working in politics and Amandine Ohayon, CEO of Stella McCartney addressed the Economics Society. The Iris Club used python to access Cern data and used CAD models to model the adoption of hydrogen fuel tanks to aeroplanes to minimise drag and Year 7 and 8 engaged with a robotics engineering challenge. Each year we seek to provide a number of such bespoke events in order to augment our student’s understanding of the range of opportunities they can engage with post school.
Our Year 10 pupils have some dedicated time off-timetable during National Careers Week each year to engage in a variety of sessions including: how to use Labour Market Information, Degree Apprenticeships, how to use a summer holiday and careers in Medicine and related industries. They also have the opportunity to attend subject specific enrichment sessions where they explore a certain aspect of a subject they enjoy in a more seminar style environment which is more typical of sixth form lessons. Year 10 also engaged in a TedEd project which fosters many career ready skills.
Encounters with employers happen throughout the year in Clubs and Societies. Year 10 and 12 prospective journalists had a problem statement set by Reuters to make their website more appealing to young people for example.
Work Experience
Year 11 and Year 12 pupils typically undertake work experience during the summer holidays. The Gatsby Benchmarks, which are the industry standard for careers education, recommend students have two weeks of engagement with the world of work before leaving school.
The Careers Co-ordinator helps pupils to consider how to source meaningful work experience. Students will have sessions on CV writing to assist with this and opportunities will be shared on google classroom. Pupils keep records of their interactions with the world of work, carefully considering what they have learned from their experiences.
Individual Advice
G&LFutures
The G&LFutures Programme consists of a series of projects that help students develop the skills they will need as they embark on their careers such as problem-solving, creative thinking, entrepreneurship, communication skills, and ideation.

History Tradition and Heritage
The Godolphin and Latymer School is a day school for 800 girls aged between 11 and 18. It began in 1861 as the Godolphin School, a boys’ boarding school set in fields near the River Thames in Hammersmith. Our main buildings date from this time. The boys’ school did not thrive, however, and in 1905 a new independent day school for girls was created on the same site. Support from the Latymer foundation resulted in a new name: the Godolphin and Latymer School.
Following the end of the Second World War and the transformational Education Act of 1944, Dame Joyce Bishop (Head from 1935 to 1963) took the decision that Godolphin and Latymer should become a state grammar school. Thus it was free to offer places to bright girls totally regardless of their parents’ background or income. Dame Joyce’s vision resonates strongly with the school today:
‘Each member of this new community of schools has its own function to perform, its own gifts to offer. For us, it is to foster scholarship and sound learning, to follow knowledge like a shooting star and to offer humbly an imaginative understanding of our fellow creatures born of this pursuit of wisdom, a charity that rejoices in the truth. Surely all this must continue to flourish and to gain fresh vitality as we open wider our window of experience and share with all schools the task of educating the nation.’
In 1977 grammar school status was removed from many London schools and Godolphin and Latymer reverted to the independent sector.
Subsequent years have seen a growth in numbers, much modernisation in educational outlook, and the imaginative development of our Hammersmith site. We enjoy our history, but our eyes always look towards the future!
1905 Godolphin and Latymer Founded
Godolphin School for boys, which had been founded in 1861, was re-opened as a girls’ school in 1905. Its name was changed to the Godolphin and Latymer School.
1910 Old Dolphin's Association Formed
The head, Miss Gertrude Clement, reported that the ODA was 'strong and lusty' in 1916 with over 200 members who met regularly, enjoyed a weekly OD gym class, lectures and playing school teams at hockey.
1913 Christmas Bazaar raised money for a school organ
The first Christmas bazaar, offered ‘attractive and inexpensive Christmas presents for sale’ together with ‘numerous entertainments and sideshows’. The large sum of £377 was raised towards the new organ, which was unveiled the following year.
1931 Franc Ha Leal Fund started
This fund helped current and former Dolphins who were facing financial hardship in the Depression. The annual school fete each summer was a major source of income, along with small envelopes tucked into school reports inviting contributions.
1950 Gymnasium re-opened after wartime bomb damage
The Head, Dame Joyce Bishop, led a campaign appealing to parents, Old Dolphins and friends of the school to raise the £4100 needed to re-build the gym, which had suffered bomb damage in the war.
1955 School Jubilee celebrated
A commemorative book was published to mark the school’s 50th anniversary. Old Dolphins attending the celebratory events donated to the Jubilee Fund for new staging and curtains for the Hall and for furnishings for the staffroom.
1977 Bursary Fund launched
Godolphin and Latymer became fully independent, rather than remain in the state sector as a non-selective school. A Bursary Fund was established to ensure that bright girls could continue to attend whatever their circumstances.
1991 Art, Science and Technology block opened
A new three-storey building was constructed to house the Art, Science and Technology departments, and was opened by the Rt Hon Chris Patten MP. Old Dolphins and other friends of the school had raised £500,000 towards the new block and an auction of promises had attracted generous bids for the head to wash a car!
2004 Annual Fund launched
The Annual Fund was launched in 2004 (and continues today). Its inaugural project was to provide floodlighting for the sports pitches.
2006 Opening of the Margaret Gray Building
The conversion of the former vicarage on Iffley Road generated extra classroom space, particularly for sixth form teaching, and provided further staff offices.
2008 The Rudland Music School
New facilities provided the Music department with teaching and rehearsal spaces, eighteen practice rooms, a recording studio and technology centre, and a Music library.
2009 The Bishop Centre
The former church of St John the Evangelist, designed by William Butterfield in 1858, was converted to create a flexible performance space for large scale events. A highly versatile lighting rig, acoustic blinds and a movable floor mean that concerts, dance or theatre can be put on in a wide range of different formats.
2015 The Hampton Sport and Fitness Centre
The new sports centre boasts a dance studio, climbing wall, fitness suite, and multi-sport hall. The facilities allow the Godolphin pupils to take their sport to new levels, and are also shared with local primary schools.
2023 Extended Sixth Form Centre
The newly extended and refurbished Sixth Form Centre opened in September 2023 providing our eldest students with a light and modern space for relaxation and private study. The reconfiguration also allows for direct links to the library and study rooms in the new Alison Paines Building.
2024 Alison Paines Building
The Alison Paines Building opened in January 2024. The new Cloisters Room on the ground floor provides additional dining facilities and space for assemblies, workshops, lectures, talks and meetings. The new, modern Library is now situated on the two floors above and is beautifully designed with a central staircase and incorporates a Seminar Room and private study area. The courtyards and outdoor spaces were also redesigned and landscaped and the new building is better connected to existing buildings.

Art & DesignDesign and Creativity
Art and Design is extremely popular at Godolphin both as an academic subject but also as part of the extra-curricular programme. Students take advantage of the fantastic facilities housed in five studio classrooms including a pottery with it’s own potters wheels and kiln and darkroom. We offer all Art and Design specialisms and work broadly across ceramics, cold glass, painterly applications, photography, and printmaking – we have huge 3D printer – sculpture, textiles, and fashion.
The annual Lower School Art and Design Exhibition is a highlight of the school calendar featuring work from every single student in Years 7 – 9. This year’s theme is Spectacular Structures and previous years have included Takeaway Food and Crufts. There are also annual exhibitions from our GCSE, A Level and IB artists.
Extra-curricular activities include art clubs that focus on 3D design, photography, ceramics, textiles, and sculpture. Trips include visits to the National Portrait Gallery; Tate Gallery; Worthing beach; Design Museum; The Welcome Trust, Emirates Air Line cable cars; and the CASS Sculpture Foundation.
We have a very strong cohort of students who study GCSE, A level and IB art and each year we offer art scholarships at Sixth Form.

Student LeadershipCompassionate Leadership and Change-Makers
Throughout their school life, students at Godolphin and Latymer are encouraged to take a lead on issues that matter to them; there is a real emphasis on developing girls’ ability to lead and make things happen. In addition to our Head Girls Team, House Captains, Games and Sports Captains, there are a number of other key leadership roles, for example Theatre and Technical Captains and Debating Captains. Our student-led committees such as the school council, diversity committee and sustainability committee play an important role in planning and running school activities that help shape and develop the culture and ethos of our school.
At the beginning of the academic year, Upper Sixth students in positions of responsibility undertake leadership development training to help them, as people and as teams, work towards producing their desired outcomes for the year. In 2024 we partnered with Isar Bhattachrjee, an organisational psychologist and founder of Uncover Consulting, and the girls spent the morning on various immersive activities.
